$doc: Hand-pinned matcher verdicts. Ruled by the review lead on 2026-09-02, in the round that
ratified R14 (spec.md §10) — the specific-beats-general resolution flip.
AUTHORITY. These carry exactly the authority of the 54 `matcherCollisions` verdicts in
inventory/core-tier.json: tools/build-theme.mjs resolves both BEFORE any precedence rule,
so a pin wins over tier, over rank, over source count and over id order, in either
resolution mode. The two sets are merged into one map and must not disagree; if the same
matcher appears in both with different winners the build fails rather than picking one.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. R14 is a TIER rule, and a tier is not a measurement of specificity.
It is right 194 times out of 205. It is wrong wherever an upstream source theme gave a
narrow concept an over-broad matcher — Material's `qwik` claiming `.tsx` outright,
vsicons' `esphome` claiming `.yaml` — because the tier arithmetic cannot tell that from a
genuinely specific claim. A pin is the per-matcher correction, and it is deliberately data
and not code: the rule stays one line in build-theme.mjs, and the exceptions are a list
anyone can read. `theme/resolution-flip-diff.md` §3 is where new candidates come from.
THE RULE THE PINS BELOW ENCODE. Two shapes, both from that diff's sanity scans:
1. EPONYMOUS (§3b) — a matcher whose value IS a concept's own id belongs to that
concept. `.xml` is xml's, `components/` is components'. Nothing more specific can
exist, so no precedence rule may take it away.
2. BLAST RADIUS (§3c) — a matcher that a top-ranked core concept covers in the real
world stays with it unless the challenger is genuinely narrower. `.tsx` is React's,
`.cls` is a LaTeX class far more often than a VB class module.
FORMAT. `matcher` is `kind:value`, the same syntax core-tier.json uses, with kind one of
ext | name | lang | dir. `winner` is a concept id, and it MUST be one of the concepts that
actually claims that matcher — build-theme.mjs validates every pin against the claim map
and fails on a typo rather than silently ignoring it. `over` names who the pin beats, and
`keeps` records what each loser still resolves through, so a pin can never quietly strand
an icon without that being written down here.
COST, RECORDED. Three concepts lose their only matcher to these pins and become
unreachable: file/qwik, folder/ngrx-store and folder/redux-store. That is not an oversight
— see their `keeps` fields. The merged inventory gives each of them nothing but the
matcher pinned away, so the choice was between a wrong icon on a common path and no icon
on a rare one. folder/store, which the flip had stranded, is recovered by the same pins.

pins.why: Blast radius, the largest in the set: reactts is core rank 2 and .tsx is the React TypeScript component extension. Material's qwik concept claims the extension outright, which is an over-broad upstream matcher, not a narrower reading.
pins.keeps: qwik keeps NOTHING — ext:tsx is its only matcher, so this pin strands file/qwik. Accepted: a Qwik repo is .tsx files that are React-shaped anyway, and the alternative paints every TSX file in every React repo as Qwik.

pins.why: Eponymous: .yaml is yaml's own id, and yaml is core rank 12. Both challengers are vsicons device-config concepts that claim the bare extension.
pins.keeps: esphome keeps lang:esphome; homeassistant keeps lang:home-assistant. Both stay reachable.

pins.why: The other half of the same concept — .yml is the same file as .yaml and belongs to the same icon. cloudfoundry claiming the bare extension is the same over-broad upstream matcher.
pins.keeps: cloudfoundry keeps name:.cfignore and lang:manifest-yaml. Stays reachable.

pins.why: Eponymous: .xml is xml's own id, and xml is core rank 27. `source` is a broader concept than xml, not a narrower one — the flip's plainest inversion.
pins.keeps: source keeps ext:axml, ext:pex and ext:xaml. Stays reachable.

pins.why: Same verdict on the language id, so the extension and the language cannot disagree about what an XML file looks like.
pins.keeps: source keeps ext:axml, ext:pex and ext:xaml. Stays reachable.

pins.why: TikZ is a TeX drawing package; .tikz is a TeX file. matlab's claim on it is an upstream mis-claim, not a specific reading.
pins.keeps: matlab keeps 16 matchers including ext:m, ext:mat, ext:fig, ext:slx and lang:matlab. Stays reachable.

pins.why: The LaTeX class file is the common .cls by a wide margin, and tex already owns the family (.sty, .dtx, .bib all resolve there). Three concepts claim the extension; none of them is narrower than the others, so the tie goes to the most common reading.
pins.keeps: apex keeps lang:apex; vba keeps lang:vba; vb keeps ext:bas, ext:doccls, ext:frm, ext:vb, lang:vb and lang:visualbasic. All three stay reachable.

pins.why: Eponymous: components/ is the components folder's own id, and it is core rank 8. A bare components/ directory is framework-agnostic — it is as likely to be Svelte, Angular or plain HTML as React.
pins.keeps: react-components keeps dir:jsx, dir:react, dir:react-components and dir:reactjs, and stays reachable. The vue FOLDER concept has no emblem on disk at all — it is one of the 56 folder concepts R9 leaves on the canon tan pair — so it had nothing to lose here and the pin costs it nothing.

pins.why: Eponymous: services/ is the services folder's own id. `controller` claiming it is an upstream MVC over-reach — a services/ directory is not a controllers directory.
pins.keeps: controller keeps 15 matchers including dir:controller, dir:controllers, dir:handler, dir:handlers and dir:provider. Stays reachable.

pins.why: A bare store/ directory is generic. Five concepts claim it and none of them can tell from the directory name alone whether it is NgRx, Redux, Vuex, Pinia or a data-access layer, so it goes to the generic store bag.
pins.keeps: db keeps 14 matchers including dir:data, dir:database, dir:db and dir:repository. ngrx-store keeps NOTHING (dir:store is its only matcher) and redux-store keeps NOTHING once dir:stores is pinned too; both are stranded by this pin, deliberately. vuex-store was already unreachable before the pin, for the same reason.

pins.why: The plural of the same generic directory, pinned to the same icon so store/ and stores/ cannot render as two different things.
pins.keeps: db keeps 14 other matchers. redux-store and vuex-store keep nothing beyond dir:store, which is pinned by the row above — see its `keeps`.
